question: Does the documented pipeline rebuild the native image in use?
method: tools/prepare_pi_cam_source.py into a fresh tree, compared against the tree the image in use was built from
validation/jobs/pi_cam_promoted_statepool_build.pbs with FREECAM_IMAGE_ROOT and FREECAM_PREPARED_SOURCE pointed at scratch, so the image in use was not replaced
compared: manifest commands, compiled objects, exported symbols, ELF sections
reused_not_rebuilt: the oracle CESM case bld/lib/libatm.a -- the pipeline links the oracle's own objects by design; rebuilding them would move the numerical boundary and require a new 512-rank bit-for-bit gate

prepared_source.note: byte-identical otherwise; the record now names 12 applied patches and 10 installed support modules, where the previous hand-kept list named 10 patches and no support modules

commands.difference: the -o path and the working directory only

conclusion: The pipeline reproduces the image. Every compile and link command is identical once the build roots are normalised, all 34 compiled objects have byte-identical .text, and the linked artifacts export identical symbol sets. The linked files differ only in .debug_str/.debug_line/.trace, which embed the build's own paths, and in the addresses those sections shift.
